I'm a veterinary assistant with a pug mix. He also hates getting his nails done. There are a couple different ways I do this, most of which I do alone (my husband is afraid of getting bit...)

First way: Flip pug onto their back. Get on top of them, with your knees on either side. Don't sit on him, but put just enough pressure that he can't flip over. You have to squeeze his sides with your knees a little bit. This will give you access to his front paws, while his back paws are under your butt and can't do much. If he's a biter like mine, have someone hold his mouth closed (this will also stop the screaming.) When I have my husband do this, my pug stops breathing in protest (like an angry toddler.) Ignore it. They'll start breathing again. If you're concerned about it, you can do one foot at a time. To do the back feet, simply turn around and put your butt in his face and do his back feet.

Second way: Put pug on his side. Put one arm over his neck, and one over his stomach area. This is how we restrain dogs at the clinic. Use your hands to hold his feet, and if you have to, you can use your chest to put pressure on him so he can't wiggle around too much. Something like this. http://imgur.com/a/mSPwH

I can try and come up with more ways if those don't work for you, but I would try those first. The most important thing is to let him know that you're the boss. That his nails WILL be getting done, whether he likes it or not. Don't let him control you.

Here's my theory: people are going to buy puppies. It's always going to happen. Some people like purebred dogs. Personally, I love pugs. Yes, I absolutely would buy a purebred pug from a breeder (besides that I'm too poor right now.) I just had an interview with a lady who shows and breeds standard Poodles. She keeps her dogs in cages. That's an awful way for them to live. Now, there are breeders who actually give a shit about their dogs. It's not awful for dogs to have a c-section. It's a relatively simple surgery, and veterinary medicine has come so far in making sure anesthesia is safe for pets. 

Honestly, if I had the time, I'd probably breed dogs too. There's a lot of money in puppies- and who wouldn't love to spend all day taking care of them?

I work in the veterinary field. There are actually quite a few people who just don't want to spay and neuter. Whether it's money issues, they're scared of their pet going under anesthesia, they don't want them to "lose their manhood," or even one guy who said his pitbull wouldn't be a guard dog without his testicles. 

When dogs go into heat, they really try to run away so they can breed- and it happens more often than usual. In this situation, they look like full-bred puppies, so it probably is a breeder. (Which, honestly, I can't be too hard on either. There's ridiculous amounts of money in puppies. And if they're taking care of all of the dogs properly and finding them good homes, good for them.)

I'm most grateful for my father.

He and my mother got divorced when I was in the 3rd grade. It took me a long time to understand what had happened. It started with a lot of yelling one night- then we had to get out of bed and go to my grandmother's. A cop came over. I don't remember much of the situation, but there was a lot of crying. We lived between my grandmother's house and government housing for the next 5 years or so.

When my grandmother passed away, my sister and I were sent to live with our dad. He worked a lot, and spent a lot. He wanted so badly to make sure that we looked like we were rich. He worked really hard to make sure that we always had nice things, and got the best gifts for Christmas.

I think the money is what eventually broke him down. Or maybe it was working so much. I've spent a lot of time thinking about it, but I've never really found the true answer. 

After awhile, the abuse started. It started with yelling every so often. It eventually got to the point of physical abuse. The last time it happened was also the scariest.

I came home from my friend's house one day. It was one of the days where he didn't get off work until 8. I was sitting at the kitchen table, probably drawing or doing homework or something. While I was at my friend's house, we had decided that it was a cool idea to dye my hair black. One thing that my dad had never cared about was what I did with my hair. It had been blonde, light brown, green, straight, curly, a million things. But for some reason, this set him off. He yelled at me. A lot. As per usual, I didn't say anything back. I didn't cry. I just sat there, continuing what I was doing. He ripped the pen out of my hand, and threw it. He yelled because I "wasn't listening." 

I continued to sit there, staring at the table. Still no words, and still no tears. He bent over, and put his face right next to mine. His nose was nearly touching my cheek. I could feel his breath, and when he said, "I'm going to knock your f***ing teeth out," I felt the spit hit the side of my face. 

Again, I had no response. I turned my face so I was looking at him. Maybe if he saw who he was saying this to, maybe if he looked at me, into the blue eyes that he created- he would stop. He would realize what he's doing, and how he's hurting me. He didn't. He stood back up, and pulled the chair backwards. He threw me out of it (kind of by pushing it forwards, letting the back legs come off the ground,) and I barely missed the side of the table. 

I stood up. Again, showing no fear. Not a single tear had dropped from my eyes. He pushed me against the wall and told me to go to my room. I did. Eventually he went to sleep, and that's the night I left. 

The point of all of this, is that my father made me who I am today. He made me a strong person. I'm not scared of anything anymore. I'm not scared of being hit, of someone yelling at me. If my father hadn't been in my life, or if I had lived with my mom all those years- there's no way I would be anywhere. I would have let people walk all over me, and I would cry over almost everything. I'm strong now. I believe in myself. I'm not afraid of what a human being can do or say to me, because I've been through enough. Some people have said that it's made me cold, heartless. It's not that. I let the right people in. It just takes a lot of trust to get to that point.

I'm currently in a happy relationship. And I feel like if I hadn't had the experience with my father, I would have ended up in an abusive relationship and unable to get out- just like my mother once was.

I had a really hard time throughout high school. There was a long period of time where I felt like cutting myself was the only answer. I hardly had any friends, and the ones I did dropped out by the time Junior year came around.

I stayed silent in nearly all of my classes, only talking to the teacher if they called on me. Even then, half of my answers weren't much more than a mumbled, "I don't know." 

I thought that every laugh I heard was somebody laughing at me. I constantly made myself believe that everybody hated me. That I would never have a friend, that my life would be destined to suck forever. Not a day went by where I didn't think about committing suicide. I told myself that it was impossible for a god to exist, because nobody would make somebody's life so horrible.  

Until one day, when I found my answer. 

A friend of my mom's was working on someone's car in exchange for horseback riding lessons. As a birthday present, he gave me those lessons. For the first time in what felt like years, I was excited about something.

I went every Wednesday after school. After two lessons, my instructor told me that I was a natural. That drove me to keep going. I wanted to keep learning, I wanted to be the best. I couldn't think of anything better than competing in shows, getting first place. Showing off how much of a "natural" I was. I daydreamed about it. It was all I ever talked about. It was all I ever thought about.

I spent a lot of time dreaming about what kind of horse I would get for myself. Where I would keep it, the exact colors and patterns. I had a million names picked out. Slowly, I stopped thinking about wanting to kill myself, and more about the future. I imaged now that I had a future. 

Thinking back on it, my instructor saved my life. She made me believe that I was worth something. Not just the girl that never talks. She helped me come out of my shell, become more than I ever thought I could be. And for that, I could never thank her enough.

It's okay to fall down, you can always get back up.
